span.label: THE DOUBLE DISSOCIATION ITSELF, and it is two CURVES rather than two conditions: `within the SOA range from 42 to 98 ms: the amount of priming INCREASED, but recognition accuracy DETERIORATED with SOA`. No level of invisibility is asserted anywhere - the argument is carried entirely by the opposite slopes, which is the criterion Schmidt2011 later proposed as a replacement for requiring zero sensitivity
span.quote: For 42-ms primes and masks, there was a remarkable double dissociation within the SOA range from 42 to 98 ms: the amount of priming increased, but recognition accuracy deteriorated with SOA

span.label: `DIFFERENT TEMPORAL LAWS` - the general form of the claim, and it is a statement about SHAPES rather than about magnitudes: conscious perception and unconscious behavioural effects of the same masked stimuli do not merely differ in size, they are governed by different functions of time. Seventh record this sitting where a time course is the load-bearing variable, and the first where two time courses ARE the finding
span.quote: Over a wide range of time courses, we show that conscious perception and unconscious behavioral effects of masked visual stimuli obey different temporal laws

span.label: SUBLIMINAL IN WHICH RESPECT - a precision most records in this corpus do not make: `prime stimuli were NOT subliminal in the sense that their presence or absence could not be detected, but the CRITICAL PRIME FEATURE remained perfectly invisible`. Something was plainly there to be seen; the attribute that did the priming was not. `Subliminal` is a predicate of a FEATURE here, not of a stimulus, and the difference decides what the effect is evidence for
span.quote: Note that prime stimuli were not subliminal in the sense that their presence or absence could not be detected, but the critical prime feature remained perfectly invisible

span.label: the priming time course is INDIFFERENT to whether the prime could be reported: `We observed priming with IDENTICAL TIME COURSE for reportable and invisible prime stimuli, despite qualitative changes in the masking time course.` The masking function changes shape - type A to type B - and the priming function does not follow it. That is a stronger result than a difference in size at one delay, because it survives a change in the shape of the other curve
span.quote: We observed priming with identical time course for reportable and invisible prime stimuli, despite qualitative changes in the masking time course

span.label: extends → the neural accumulator model of Hanes and Schall
span.quote: It is similar to the neural accumulator model of Hanes and Schall (26) but includes saturation in the stochastic accumulation process

span.quote: These findings do not agree with central notions of Milner and Goodale ’s theory (3), such as the role of color processing in the action system and the importance of hard-wired connections to effectors

span.note: differs in: THEIR TIME COURSES - measured under the same conditions, on the same stimuli, and found to obey different temporal laws. Over 42 to 98 ms priming rises while recognition falls, so neither can be a noisier reading of the other · strength of the relation: 0.95 — THE PAPER'S RESULT, and the empirical basis for the criterion Schmidt2011 proposes eight years later. Confidence 0.95 - the contrast is the study's design, stated in its own summary of what it did.
span.quote: We manipulated the visibility of masked stimuli and contrasted it with their inﬂuence on the speed of motor actions, comparing the temporal dynamics of visual awareness in metacontrast masking with that of action priming under the same conditions

span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — Half of the dissociation. Recorded separately from the visibility half so that the two directions are queryable independently - a corpus that stored only `there was a double dissociation` could not answer which way each curve went.
span.quote: For 42-ms primes and masks, there was a remarkable double dissociation within the SOA range from 42 to 98 ms: the amount of priming increased, but recognition accuracy deteriorated with SOA

span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.9 — The other half, and the reason the pair is a dissociation rather than a correlation: the SAME manipulation moves the two measures in OPPOSITE directions over the same interval.

span.quote: Priming may occur without awareness of the prime, as has been shown in neurological patients (3–5) and healthy subjects (6–10).
